perf-bot: ALERT: spike detected — p99 latency 2.3x above baseline for model redwood-abc-1.4-quant in us-west-2 (hosts: gpu-pool-7). Trigger: rollout started 1758198000.

leo: seeing this too. spike started ~10:02 UTC after the tokenizer tweak landed in the rollout. :eyes: 

marta: KV cache hit rate on affected hosts dropped from ~85% -> ~23% around the same time. logs show more unique prefix hashes.

aj: can you paste profiler traces? nvprof / runtime profiler would help.

marta: put a short dump below from runtime-profiler for a slow request:

```
request_id=ab12c
model=redwood-abc-1.4-quant
seq_len=768
kernel_selected=matmul_kernel_v2
batch_size=1
gpu_time_ms=18.2
cpu_prep_ms=12.5
kv_cache_hit=false
backend_queue_ms=42.1
total_latency_ms=82.9
```

marta: contrast with baseline (old tokenizer + model v1.3):

```
seq_len=128
kernel_selected=matmul_kernel_smallbatch
batch_size=4
gpu_time_ms=4.1
kv_cache_hit=true
total_latency_ms=18.7
```

sara: so tokenizer change increased tokenization length skew -> more long-tail seqs -> kernel chooser picks the wrong heavy kernel and batching heuristics collapse to small batch sizes. also kv cache miss increased because prefixes differ slightly.

aj: I dug into kernel selector logs. It switches to matmul_kernel_v2 for seq_len >= 512 by policy. But v2 has worse startup latency for batch_size<=2 (we saw perf regression in bench run on quantized kernels). The rollout increased proportion of requests with seq_len in [512,900], so tail proportion jumped.

leo: noisy neighbor effect as well — same hosts saw other tenants bursty workloads, pushing our scheduler to de-schedule background batching threads. But primary cause looks model/tokenizer -> seq distribution shift.

oncall: mitigation options? rollback tokenizer, change kernel selection thresholds, or force smallbatch kernel for quantized profiles.

marta: I pushed a quick canary patch to runtime to bias kernel chooser:

```
// tmp hotfix: prefer smallbatch kernel for quantized models when batch_size <= 2
if (model.is_quantized && batch_size <= 2) kernel = smallbatch_kernel;
```

marta: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2456

aj: rolling patch to us-west-2 canary (2 hosts) now. will monitor KV hit rate and p99.

perf-bot: UPDATE: canary hosts show p99 reduced from 310ms -> 95ms after patch. KV hit still low but kernel path improved tail.

sara: longer term we need:
- update kernel selection to use joint cost model (seq_len distribution + expected batch priming cost)
- expression-level tokenizer compatibility tests to catch prefix-shift regressions
- gating rollout by KV-hit rate for stateful LLM serving

leo: agreed. also add a perf regression test in CI: quantized model + tokenizer variants with synthetic seq distribution.

marta: created ticket INF-922: "Kernel selector cost-model + rollout gates for KV-hit & seq-dist". assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

aj: action items now:
1) finish canary rollout of hotfix (in progress) — aj
2) rollback tokenizer if canary fails — leo
3) implement KV prefix fingerprinting metric in console — marta
4) add CI perf test path — sara

sara: small note: disable aggressive prefix normalization in tokenizer v1.4 until we do compatibility testing.

leo: thanks everyone. I'll follow up in the incident doc with timeline and RCA once we have postmortem numbers. :thumbsup: 

marta: attaching sample KV hit dump for one host (time series):

```
2025-09-18T10:00Z kv_hit=0.85
2025-09-18T10:05Z kv_hit=0.82
2025-09-18T10:10Z kv_hit=0.24  <-- rollout start
2025-09-18T10:15Z kv_hit=0.22
2025-09-18T10:25Z kv_hit=0.27  <-- canary patch applied
2025-09-18T10:35Z kv_hit=0.29
```

aj: will post perf counters + flamegraph later in the thread. for now dashboard alerts suppressed to avoid paging duplicates.

perf-bot: RESOLVED (partial): canary shows improvement, ramp paused. monitoring continues.
